scenes.name: Grunge y rock alternativo
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Nevermind de Nirvana (noviembre de 1991) llega al número uno el 11 de enero de 1992 y acaba con el reinado del lite metal. Los medios abrazan a Kurt Cobain y Eddie Vedder, las radios crean formatos «alternativos», la gran emisora de metal de Los Ángeles, KNAC, se vende en 1995 y MTV cancela Headbangers Ball en 1996; hasta Kerrang! se abre a la nueva moda, y los críticos, que crecieron con el rock universitario, ven por fin validado su gusto. El grunge no es metal aunque comparte la guitarra y la voz fuerte: alterna partes duras y suaves, canta el dolor y la desesperación, viste de tienda de segunda mano e identifica a la generación X con los débiles, frente al poder y el placer del metal («Somos pesados, pero no heavy metal», dice Krist Novoselic). Hacia 1998 el alternativo está moribundo.

podcast.title: Eyes Adrift Formation and Disbandment
podcast.body: Following Sweet 75, Chris formed Eyes Adrift with a member of the Meat Puppets (one of Nirvana's favorite bands) and the drummer from Sublime. This band also failed to attract an audience and was finished by 2003. "That was followed by a group called Eyes Adrift, with a guy from the Meet Puppets, one of Nirvana's favorite bands, and the drummer from Sublime."

podcast.title: Political Activism
podcast.body: Chris Novoselic is heavily involved in regional politics, with a particular focus on electoral reform. "Chris's big thing is Electoral Reform, and in 2004 he wrote a wafer-thin book called of Grunge and Government."

podcast.title: Post-Nirvana Musical Ventures
podcast.body: After Kurt Cobain's death, Chris Novoselic attempted to continue his musical career with several bands, but none achieved significant success. "Chris Nova Selich, the guy everyone thought would be the person to carry on Nirvana's musical legacy, tried to keep things going with a couple of bands, but things just didn't work out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Roadie for The Melvins
podcast.body: Krist Novoselic, known for his work with Nirvana, also served as a roadie for The Melvins during the pre-grunge era in Seattle, alongside Kurt Cobain. "Kurt Cobain worked as a roadie for the Melvins, so to Christ Novicellech."

podcast.title: Solo Album Rumors and Flipper Stint
podcast.body: Rumors of a Chris Novoselic solo album in 2005 were interrupted by a stint with the old-school punk band Flipper. He planned to record an album with Flipper, but in September 2008, he cancelled all tours and the album was never recorded due to his increasing responsibilities at home and involvement in regional politics. "There were rumblings of a Christian of a solid solo album in 2005, but that was interrupted by a stint with an old-school punk band called Flipper."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Speculated Post-Nirvana Life (if Kurt Lived)
podcast.body: It is speculated that if Kurt had lived and pursued an acoustic career, Chris Novoselic would have continued to follow his political interests, potentially sticking with Kurt to support him. "Chris Nova Selich. Well, he was always the activist of the band, the political guy. So as Dave went off with the food fighters and Kurt became this accoustic guy, I could still see Chris following his political interests."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sweet 75 Formation and Disbandment
podcast.body: He formed Sweet 75 in late 1995 with Venezuelan street musician Yiva Las Vegas. Despite a debut album in 1997, it "just kind of disappeared" due to its experimental alt-pop sound. Plans for future albums in late 1999 and early 2001 fell apart, leading to the band's demise. "First, he was in a band called Sweet 75 through late 1995. The singer was a street musician from Venezuela who went by the name of Yiva Las Vegas."

xref.title: European Tour Cancellation (March 1994)
xref.body: Following their performance at Terminal 1 in Munich on March 1, 1994, the remainder of Nirvana's European tour was cancelled. This decision was made because Kurt Cobain was deemed unfit to continue, suffering from bronchitis and a sore throat. The other band members, Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl, also needed a vacation, with Novoselic returning to Seattle and Grohl remaining in Germany to work on a film soundtrack. "After that show, the rest of the European tour was cancelled."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Intervention and Brief Rehab Stay (March 25-April 1, 1994)
xref.body: On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held for Kurt Cobain, involving Nirvana members Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl, guitarist Pat Smear, management and legal team members, doctors, and drug counselor James Burr. The five-hour meeting persuaded Kurt to enter rehab, and he communicated his intention to rest and recover via his AOL account. On March 30, he checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles but departed just two days later on April 1, scaling a guard wall despite having checked in voluntarily. "That meeting lasted five hours. Kurt was convinced to try rehab and arrangements were made."

xref.title: Beliefs of Family and Bandmates on Cause of Death
xref.body: Close associates of Kurt Cobain, including his Nirvana bandmates Dave Grohl and Krist Novoselic, his mother, his father, and two of his managers, all believe that he died by suicide. Their consensus reflects the official conclusion of the Seattle Police Department and King County Medical Examiner's office. "Dave Grohl believes Kurt killed himself. Chris Novicellich believes Kurt killed himself."

xref.title: Chad Channing's Drumming Tenure – Introduction by a Friend
xref.body: Chad Channing became Nirvana's drummer for a period after a friend introduced him to Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic. Prior to this, Channing had been playing in a band called Tick Dolly Roe with Ben Shepherd, whose departure to Nirvana led to the end of Tick Dolly Roe. "One of Chad's friends introduced him to Kurt Cobain and Chris Nova Selaich, and he became Nirvana's drummer for a while."

xref.title: Ended by Drummer's Departure to Nirvana – Impact of Chad Channing
xref.body: Tick Dolly Roe was a band that included Ben Shepherd and Chad Channing. The group dissolved after Channing was introduced to Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic by a friend and subsequently became Nirvana's drummer for a while. "So that was it for Tick Tock Dolly, but Ben Shepard didn't mind, because he freelanced as Nirvana's Rody for a while."

xref.title: Krist Novoselic – Name History from Croatian Birth Spelling to English Variations
xref.body: Born May 16, 1965 to Croatian immigrant parents, Krist's birth name was spelled "Krste" in the Old World Croatian way (his father's name being Kristo). At school the name was Anglicized to "Chris" (C-H-R-I-S). At age 15 in 1980, he attended a Croatian high school in Zadar on the Adriatic coast, where classes included assembling and disassembling a machine gun as part of civil defense training. Returning to Aberdeen, he favored "Krist" (K-R-I-S-T) again. Early Nirvana materials often credited him as "Chris Novoselic" (likely a record company decision), but from *Nevermind* onward it has been "Krist." Anyone calling him "Chris" was corrected. "Novoselic was a fairly unusual name for Croatian and Serbian — it meant 'new villager.'"

xref.title: Only Nirvana Song Without Kurt Cobain's Performance
xref.body: "Marigold" is the only officially released Nirvana song where Kurt Cobain does not play on the track. It is a Dave Grohl composition, recorded during the *In Utero* sessions by Grohl (drums, guitars, vocals) and Krist Novoselic (bass). "Officially that's an Nirvana song but Kurt Cobain does not play on the track It's a Dave Grohl composition called Merrigold"
